disease_label_per_paper: Enterococcus faecalis bacteremia with infective endocarditis, septic coronary embolus, splenic infarct, and rectosigmoid perforation source
presentation_summary: 69-year-old woman with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, obesity with gastric band, and breast cancer history was airlifted after waking with chest pain, shortness of breath, and diaphoresis.
Initial ECG and troponin were consistent with STEMI; catheterization showed 100% LAD occlusion without atherosclerosis elsewhere and aspiration thrombectomy was performed.
On hospital day 2 she developed left upper quadrant abdominal pain, fever to 103 F, tachycardia, hypotension, leukocytosis, and CT evidence of splenic infarct and mild splenic-flexure thickening.
Blood cultures later grew Enterococcus faecalis; TEE later showed a mitral-valve vegetation and subsequent GI workup found rectosigmoid perforation.
